item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Like the image, but don't think "communicating" is quite the right term to use in the caption with the current version of the scip. I guess it used to be a thing what "talked" with emotions or something before, but now it's just a thing what gives you visions of the past.

In addendum 2, the guy says he woke up… Should that be changed to something similar to the first interview, or should it be noted by a researcher that the subject "snapped out of it" on his own without need for being removed from proximity to the SCP?

Subjects within the city will frequently be seen performing rituals or leaving offerings to specific statues.

Because the people being exposed to 496 are referred to as "subjects", I think that could be reworded to be a little more clear as to what it's trying to convey. Such as:

Other individuals are frequently seen within the city by subjects, performing rituals or leaving offerings to specific statues.

Was going to say neutral vote, but it's right on the cusp, so I'm just gonna give it the +1 a very minor edit would warrant. =)

E: It doesn't need to be added (because making people ask these questions is sometimes better than answering them), but the addendum about everything collapsing and being destroyed… Has anyone else had that particular experience? Does it happen every year on November 14th? Ie, the visions are on repeat, as if you're watching a replay of the final year of Atlantis.

item.content:encoded:
You have typos and the redaction isn't good at any point (even the strikethrough in the description; the sentence with a strikethrough in it should form a complete sentence if the stricken-through portion were removed). Also, the first interview log has really wonky tone; the Agent varies between casual, nonscientific tone (which one would expect him to have), talking about "the dead guy" and what not, but occasionally shifts into saying things like "But first I'd like to note that it has a very powerful ability to experience emotions, and to convey those to others" or "I tried to think thoughts of origin, and beginnings", which are both awfully clinical and pretty stilted dialogue in general.

Not a fan. Need to take down and run it through your usual editing rigor.

item.title: Re: Rewrite complete
item.content:encoded:
I can see why you'd want to make it more emotionally involving, but the first version was better. This isn't really a site where you'd write up a sob story like that. You need to enhance the horror and the creep, not the heart-wrenching.

An idea: the statue is not intelligent enough to deduce that humans cannot survive underwater, and is so desperate for company that it will capture and drown anyone who approaches. To this end, it broadcasts a psychic 'beacon' that draws humans there to investigate, at which point they are caught and drowned.

Second idea: the statue is intelligent, and malevolent. The coral it is composed of can actively colonize others on contact, and convert them to a new instance. With each added instance, the statue can remain active longer when out of contact with the sea floor. Extrapolated, with enough converted humans, the group can remain active for weeks, months, years, and free to roam on dry land. Psychic beacon optional, but would probably be pushing it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for all the feedback. I'll clinical-ize the interview section tomorrow.

I wanted to the official description to remain indifferent as to the origin of the entity, and perhaps have the Agent care more about it than she should. As for its decommissioning, I don't see any reason to keep it around, it's just a drain on SCP resources if it can be easily destroyed. I think I'll try to flesh out more of an inappropriately emotional relationship between it and the Agent, making the conflict with the decommissioning more dramatic…

I'm pretty sure I'll leave this for another day or two then take it down for a rewrite. Any other input would be wonderful in the meantime!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really don't know. On the one hand, it's kind of interesting, but on the other it's too friendly for my tastes. I feel like I'm supposed to be sad for it, but as a reader I don't find myself feeling sympathetic enough for that to carry the proper oomph as the article's driving force.

Additionally, while the idea of communication based entirely on projected images is interesting, the attempt to verbally convey esoteric concepts isn't doing the tone of your article any favors. Consider playing around with the log format to make the writing more clinical; remember that it was likely written by someone who wasn't present. Also, lose the random asterisks.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This just doesn't really do much for me. A little bit sad, but that's about it. SCPs need to be either creepy, very interesting, or very very witty. This is slightly creepy and slightly interesting but not enough of either to really grab me.

Also, why hasn't it been picked up and thrown into a containment cell somewhere to make sure it can't be moved? Leaving it out in the ocean just seems a little…silly.

Also, I found your tone to be just a teensy bit off. I agree with teaflower that the interview log needs work. Keep in mind that the Foundation uses empirical observations; there is no way to quantify "a feeling of warmth", so you may want to reword it with something along the lines of "agent was instructed to project feelings of warmth and welcome to SCP-496. Agent reported similar feelings returned, as well as images of whatever." Maybe better worded than that, but you get the idea.

So yeah, all in all a neat idea that just didn't go very far.
